ns2:course.label: Micromechanics of Materials
ns2:course.description: (T A M 490) Advanced analysis of modern engineering materials with emphasis on relating microstructural phenomena to the mechanics of material behavior: prediction of elastic and thermal properties of materials with heterogeneous microstructure (such as composites), micromechanics of failure and damage, toughening mechanisms, mechanics of phase transformations; and current topics in materials research (such as high-temperature response and ferroelasticity). Prerequisite: Undergraduate course in material sciences; TAM 551.
